clue.text: Indian city's quiet temptation after docking

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts off its end, so the last letter of the lure goes

parts.note: bait is a lure or temptation

explanation.surface: A tourist describes how the city tempts visitors once their ship has come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly Bombay, it is the largest city on India's west coast.

clue.text: No fitter state, Michael admits

indicators.note: admits means the short name lets the other word in

parts.note: Mick is a short form of Michael
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: Michael confesses that the nation is no healthier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No fitter' looks like a comparison of health; it means someone who does not fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonconformist, independent sort is someone who refuses to conform with the herd.

clue.text: Priest, and character in 23

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the description of the hero

parts.note: 23 across is Shakespeare's tragic hero, known as the Moor of Venice
N is short for and, as in rock 'n' roll
a sign is a written character or symbol

explanation.surface: A priest who is also a figure in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a written symbol, not a person in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is given to senior Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Strict or direct, you might say

indicators.note: you might say signals that the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: direct means steer, so the phrase becomes or steer

explanation.surface: Asking whether to be firm or to give direct orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe or stern in manner, so harsh and unbending.

clue.text: Academic turning nasty about censor

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the censor's name
turning here means the word for nasty is read from the end backwards

parts.note: rude can mean nasty or offensive
Cato the Elder held the office of censor in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A lecturer becomes unpleasant when objecting to a censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes EDUR, which goes 'about' CATO, the famous Roman censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic is used as a noun for a university teacher, someone who instructs.

clue.text: Reason for spitting feathers in a bad way

definitions.meaning: taken literally, feathers, or ... would make you spit

explanation.surface: Why someone is furious and in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitting feathers' is British slang for furious or very thirsty; the clue takes it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means gloomy or downcast, looking miserable.

clue.text: HEARTLESS LADY? Love this music

indicators.note: this points at the clue as shown: what is left of the woman sits in the way the words are printed

parts.note: the first two words are printed in capital letters, upper case

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of the word for a woman are taken out

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman, and a love song to go with her.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters are part of the wordplay: the heartless woman sits inside the word for how the first two words are printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean song style, originating in Trinidad, often with improvised topical lyrics.

clue.text: Sound of big cat in forest

indicators.note: Sound of says the word is said aloud

parts.note: the tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: Hearing a big cat roar in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R of the cat is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The subarctic coniferous woodland of Siberia and Canada, where Siberian tigers do live.

clue.text: Shoot the messenger

definitions.meaning: a plant stem that grows along the ground and roots

explanation.surface: The proverb about not blaming the bearer of bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: A strawberry plant sends out shoots, and a messenger runs errands.

clue.text: A point briefly pinched by masseur

definitions.text: A point briefly pinched by masseur

parts.words: A point briefly pinched by masseur
parts.note: a compass point in abbreviated form sits inside the middle of the word masseur

explanation.surface: A masseur squeezing one spot on a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' means abbreviated: the three-letter compass abbreviation sits 'pinched by' masseur, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This compass bearing lies between south and south-east.

clue.text: Beauty spot, mostly square

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the place word is kept

parts.note: a venue is a place or spot
S is an abbreviation for square, as in sq or S in measurements

explanation.surface: A beauty spot, perhaps a mole, that is roughly square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty spot' reads as one phrase, but 'Beauty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of love is a byword for a stunningly beautiful woman.

clue.text: Gold supply, one to cut in after 1984?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a well is a source or supply, of water or oil

indicators.note: to cut in means the article splits the little word in two

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A goldmine's supply and someone pushing in, set in a futuristic year.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'after' as 'in the manner of': a thing after the novel 1984 is like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes oppressive surveillance like that in the dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Dress split without purpose

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tear surrounds the goal

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
aim means purpose or goal

explanation.surface: A dress tore for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for clothing or attire.

clue.text: Set up devious plan to intercept murder

indicators.note: to intercept means the shuffled letters come between the killing word's letters

parts.note: ice is slang for kill or murder

indicators.note: devious suggests something twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook arranges a cunning scheme to stop a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murder' is the American slang verb ice, to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set up is arranged and ready, positioned where it belongs.

clue.text: A novelist can or might produce another word for 'relaxed'

indicators.note: might produce says the letters of the preceding words can be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A thesaurus question: a novelist hunting another word for relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversational tone is informal and easy-going, like chatting.

clue.text: Very easy to see a game that's open?

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game
to lance a boil is to cut it open

explanation.surface: A game that's open is obvious to spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen at a glance is instantly obvious, needing only a quick look.

clue.text: Part of snowball in hand, I've evenly splattered a coat

indicators.note: evenly means the second, fourth and sixth letters of the words are taken
splattered suggests scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a snowball fight gets snow splattered over their coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes A, D, V from 'hand, I've'; 'splattered' rearranges A COAT to OCAAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Snowball cocktail is this egg liqueur mixed with lemonade.

clue.text: A very well rigged sail in latest book

indicators.note: in means the group of pieces goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: the trend is the latest fashion
sure is an informal yes, meaning very well or certainly

indicators.note: rigged suggests rearranging, as a ship's sails are set up

explanation.surface: A yachtsman approves of a sail set up in a newly published book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very well' is the informal assent 'sure', and 'latest' is the newest fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel is a famous book.

clue.text: After bombing, sank in North America

parts.note: a la means after or in the manner of

indicators.note: bombing suggests wrecking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship sank in North America after an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is the French à la, in the style of, not a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything from America's largest state, in the far north-west, is in North America.

clue.text: One studying cold and hot parts of the sun

indicators.note: parts means the word is split open to let the two letters in

parts.note: solar means of the sun
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: An astronomer studying the cool and hot regions of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person or student who devotes time to academic study.

clue.text: Graceful mountaineer's heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a mountaineer is a climber

explanation.surface: A graceful alpinist sets off for the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and lithe, able to move and bend easily.

clue.text: Denounce what parties give constituencies?

definitions.meaning: to charge a public official formally with misconduct
every constituency gets one member of parliament

explanation.surface: A cynic accusing politicians of handing out favours to constituencies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain each constituency elects one MP, a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring formal charges against an official is to accuse or condemn them.

clue.text: The Brownshirts were effectively a mob

definitions.meaning: split as ..., the Brownshirts came before the SS, Hitler's elite corps

explanation.surface: A historian calls the Nazi stormtroopers little more than a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brownshirts (SA) were the Nazi militia that preceded the SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a dense crowd of people pushing together.

clue.text: In biblical tales, how he doubted his wife

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first part of the Bible
how! is a mock greeting, so it means hello

explanation.surface: A Bible-story husband who mistrusted his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is the greeting, as in 'How!' in old Westerns, not a question word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice was tricked by Iago into suspecting Desdemona of infidelity.

clue.text: Piece of chicken covering an unfinished KFC meal

indicators.note: covering means the chicken cut wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: breast is a cut of chicken
an is the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: unfinished means the fast-food chain's initials lose their final letter

explanation.surface: Someone eating chicken from a fast-food bucket before finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: KFC is Kentucky Fried Chicken, which makes the chicken surface misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.

clue.text: McCartney's publicity nothing revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an ad is publicity, an advertisement
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A Beatle's publicity campaign turns out to be nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a woman named McCartney: Paul's first wife, the photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda Eastman married Paul McCartney in 1969, so she was a McCartney.

clue.text: Some moisture's on a teething ring

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A baby's teething ring gets slobbered on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teething ring' reads as one item, but 'ring' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to sound out and echo, as a bell's tone does.

clue.text: Dire text message to a good guy?

parts.note: U R is text-speak for you are
a gent is a gentleman, a good guy

explanation.surface: An awful text sent to a nice man.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 1,1,4 the answer is the text 'U R GENT': you are a gent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dire situation is pressing and demands immediate action.
